questions.knowledgeNote: Clear fractions first: ×3 and ×4 give 2x+3y = 48 and 4x+y = 56 — integer Cramer's rule from there.
questions.question: Q1(g). Apply matrix method or Cramer's rule: (2x/3) + y = 16; x + (y/4) = 14.
questions.solution: Multiply first by 3: 2x+3y = 48. Multiply second by 4: 4x+y = 56. D = 2(1)-3(4) = -10. Dx = 48(1)-3(56) = -120, x = 12. Dy = 2(56)-48(4) = -80, y = 8. Boxed (12,8). Verify: 8+8 = 16 ✓; 12+2 = 14 ✓ (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.10 Ex 10.3 Q1(g); book p310 = PDF p337 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2(c). Solve by matrix method or Cramer's rule: 3x - y - 2z = 1; x - y + 2z = 3; -2x + 3y + z = 8.
questions.solution: (second)-(first)÷? Use elimination: from row 2, x = 3+y-2z. In row 1: 3(3+y-2z)-y-2z = 1 gives 9+2y-8z = 1, y-4z = -4. Row 3: -2(3+y-2z)+3y+z = 8 gives -6+y+5z = 8, y+5z = 14. Subtracting: 9z = 18, z = 2; y = 14-10 = 4; x = 3+4-4 = 3. Boxed (3,4,2). Verify in first: 9-4-4 = 1 ✓ (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.10 Ex 10.3 Q2(c); book p310 = PDF p337 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Key-slip alert: 6y+6z = -1 with y = 2/3 forces z = -5/6, not +5/6 — substitution proves the printed plus is wrong.
questions.question: Q2(e). Solve by matrix method or Cramer's rule: 6y + 6z = -1; 8x + 6z = -1; 4x + 9y = 8. [Print note: the Answers line shows (1/2,2/3,5/6), but 6(2/3)+6(5/6) = 9 ≠ -1; z = -5/6 is correct.]
questions.solution: From 4x+9y = 8 and 8x+6z = -1: multiply first by 2, 8x+18y = 16; subtract second: 18y-6z = 17. With 6y+6z = -1 (×3: 18y+18z = -3): subtracting gives -24z = 20, z = -5/6. Then 6y-5 = -1, y = 2/3; 8x-5 = -1, x = 1/2. Boxed (1/2,2/3,-5/6). Verify: 4+(-5) = -1 ✓; 4-5 = -1 ✓; 2+6 = 8 ✓. The printed +5/6 fails the first equation, so it is a sign slip.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.10 Ex 10.3 Q2(e); book p310 = PDF p337 (vision read)
